title: Construction Work — Signature Rapid-Foundation Method
body: Signature edition. Signature-original construction method, created in the Signature system — presented as a Signature method, never as public record. The Signature Rapid-Foundation Method compresses footing and wall work into one continuous pour sequence using stay-in-place insulated forms. Steps: (1) excavate to a single design depth — no separate footing trench; (2) set a crushed-stone raft bed, compacted in two passes; (3) place the stay-in-place form system with its built-in drainage channel; (4) lay the Signature rebar lattice (pre-tied mats dropped in as units); (5) pour the full monolithic raft and stem walls in one day; (6) backfill the same day the forms are rated for it. The method trades deeper excavation for fewer mobilizations: one crew, one pour, one inspection. It is a Signature concept method for study and adaptation, not a code-approved public technique.
capabilities: List the pre-tied rebar lattice components
Compute stone-bed volume for the raft
Compare mobilizations vs a conventional foundation
Adapt the method to a site plan

title: Construction Work — Signature Pin-Lock Framing System
body: Signature edition. Signature-original construction method. The Pin-Lock Framing System is a Signature wood-framing variant in which studs drop into pre-slotted plates pinned with hardwood dowels, cutting nailing time at layout. Steps: (1) mill plates with slots at 16 inches on center using the Signature slot jig; (2) stand the bottom plate, anchored as usual; (3) drop studs into slots and drive the oak pin through plate and stud; (4) tip walls up and brace; (5) pin the top plate the same way. Pinning gives a mechanical lock that holds the wall square during the stand-up, after which structural screws lock it permanently. A Signature concept for study — verify with a structural engineer before any real build.
capabilities: Mill the Signature slot jig layout
Compare assembly time vs nailed framing

title: Construction Work — Signature Oul-Grid Site Layout
body: Signature edition. Signature-original layout method. 'Oul' is Manon's term, kept as named. The Signature Oul-Grid lays out a job site on a named grid of operation cells — each cell is an 'oul' — so every crew knows its working square by letter and number. Steps: (1) stake the site corners; (2) divide the site into 20-by-20-foot oul cells labeled A1, A2, B1, B2; (3) assign each operation a cell range on the layout board; (4) stage materials only inside the oul that will consume them; (5) move the day's needs list by oul, not by trade. The grid ends the classic problem of material piles blocking the next crew's work area. A Signature concept for study.
capabilities: Divide a site into oul cells
Label cells with the letter-number scheme

title: Construction Work — Signature Weather-Window Pouring
body: Signature edition. Signature-original scheduling method. Signature Weather-Window Pouring schedules concrete work around measured micro-weather instead of calendar dates. Steps: (1) log temperature, humidity, and wind on site for two weeks before the pour season; (2) define the Signature pour window (air 50-85 F, wind under 15 mph, no rain within 6 hours); (3) keep the crew on standby with a 24-hour call list; (4) trigger the pour when three consecutive readings fall inside the window; (5) protect the slab per the reading trend, not the forecast alone. The method cuts weather-damaged pours by never pouring on hope. A Signature concept for study.
capabilities: Protect slabs per the reading trend

title: Construction Work — Signature Single-Pass Rough-In
body: Signature edition. Signature-original method. The Signature Single-Pass Rough-In runs electrical and plumbing together in one coordinated pass using a shared chase plan drawn before either trade starts. Steps: (1) draw the chase plan — every vertical and horizontal run mapped on one sheet; (2) both trades pre-cut and stage their material by chase; (3) plumbing sets drains and vents first in the shared chases; (4) electrical follows in the same pass, offset per code separation; (5) one joint inspection covers both. The shared plan eliminates the classic conflict of a pipe where the panel needs to go. A Signature concept for study.
capabilities: Sequence plumbing before electrical in shared chases

title: Construction Work — Signature Punch-List Sprint
body: Signature edition. Signature-original closeout method. The Signature Punch-List Sprint closes a job in a single 48-hour burst instead of a weeks-long trickle. Steps: (1) the superintendent walks the full punch list alone and photographs every item; (2) items are grouped by trade and room into sprint cards; (3) each trade gets a card stack and a fixed 8-hour window; (4) fixes are verified by photo match before the trade leaves; (5) the final walk happens at hour 48. The fixed windows force trades to finish rather than revisit. A Signature concept for study.

title: Construction Work — Signature Material Train Delivery
body: Signature edition. Signature-original logistics method. The Signature Material Train delivers materials in work-sequence order — a 'train' of loads arriving in the exact order crews will consume them. Steps: (1) convert the work sequence into a delivery schedule; (2) load trucks in reverse order (last-needed loads first on); (3) each truck carries one operation's full needs list; (4) trucks arrive on the oul-grid call, never early; (5) packaging returns on the empty truck. The train eliminates laydown yards and double handling. A Signature concept for study.
capabilities: Convert the work sequence to a delivery schedule
Load trucks in reverse consumption order
Call trucks on the oul-grid signal

title: Construction Work — Signature Zero-Rework Inspection
body: Signature edition. Signature-original quality method. Signature Zero-Rework Inspection inspects each operation before the next one starts, so defects never get buried. Steps: (1) define the pass criteria for every operation in writing before work starts; (2) the crew lead self-checks against the criteria at day's end; (3) the superintendent signs the operation card before the next trade mobilizes; (4) any defect is fixed by the crew that made it, the same week; (5) the signed cards become the handover quality record. The rule is simple: no signed card, no next trade. A Signature concept for study.
capabilities: Assign defects to the originating crew
